# Tables the signed-in database roles (authenticated and anon) hold no INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE on, at table or column level.
# Read from production on 28-10-2026 (157 tables). A write to one of these made on the caller's own session is refused with 42501
# in production, whatever a test double accepts, so `test_a_write_of_a_table_the_signed_in_role_cannot_write_...` holds every writer
# to a client that can. A table leaves this list when a migration grants the signed-in role a write back (then its writers may use the
# caller's session); a table joins it in the migration that takes the write away. The real-Postgres half checks each name here that
# exists in the migration-built database against the privileges themselves.
# Joined by a migration in the change that moves its writers (the first line below the names is the migration): 559 closes
# receipts, receipt_allocations, purchase_payments, purchase_payment_allocations and the three note-allocation tables.
# 562 closes the seventeen
# firm-level tables of POST-A-329 (account_group_mappings, firm_hsn_library, firm_hsn_rate_history, assignment_rules, entities, entity_relationships,
# entity_to_entity_relationships, leads, dsc_records, automation_rules, automation_executions, reminder_settings, engagement_templates and the three
# recurring-template parents, task_escalations).
# 563 closes the six document headers and their six lines tables of POST-A-335 part 2 (client_sales_invoices, purchase_bills, credit_notes,
# debit_notes, purchase_credit_notes, sales_debit_notes and the six lines tables).
